audit_notes: Model: steady 1D series conduction interior -> roof (U=0.5 incl. interior film) -> aerogel mat -> aged white finish, sol-air Robin boundary; q = [alpha*I + h*dT - eps*R_net]/(1 + h*R_tot). Checks: aerogel k = 0.018 W/mK is in the range of commercial silica aerogel blankets (0.015-0.021) and published encapsulated aerogel fibres; pore size 200 nm vs air mean free path 68 nm gives Knudsen number Kn = 0.34, i.e. partial suppression of gas conduction (k_gas ~0.026/(1+2*1.6*Kn*... ) ~ 0.012 W/mK), consistent with the stated k. R_add = 0.015/0.018 = 0.83 m2K/W. Hand solution: design q = (0.33*300 + 150 - 0.9*85)/(1 + 15*2.83) = 172.5/43.5 = 3.97 W/m2; baseline (no mat) 172.5/31 = 5.56 W/m2; gain ~29 %. The gain is pure added thermal resistance; conventional PIR (k 0.022-0.025) of 20 mm would give ~0.85 m2K/W as well, at a fraction of the cost, so the lattice mainly buys thickness. Aerogel under a roof finish must be protected against water; silica aerogel is hydrophobised, but the sheath and adhesive bond under daily 30 K cycling for 20 years are unproven; compressive strength of aerogel blankets (~0.1 MPa at 10 % strain) limits foot traffic. Simulation coefficient: effective conductance 1/(R_tot + 1/h) = 0.35 W/m2K.
